newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMANY TO TAKE BACK HAZARDOUS WASTE FROM HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: GERMANY TO TAKE BACK HAZARDOUS WASTE FROM HUNGARY.

text.p: Germany acknowledged on Thursday that a shipment of 380 tonnes of hazardous waste stuck in transit in Hungary had been exported illegally, and said it would take the consignment back.
The containers were due to be shipped to China via Croatia, but Croatian authorities refused to let them cross the border.
Press reports said the shipment included six tonnes of wood preservative from the north German state of Lower Saxony and 34 tonnes of a substance used to treat the outer shell of army tanks.

"The federal government and the regional states ask Lower Saxony to coordinate the necessary return of the waste exported illegally to Hungary," said a statement issued after a meeting of officials from Bonn and Germany's federal states in Ratzeburg, northern Germany.
The statement said the return of the waste would initially be financed by a "solidarity fund" created to cope with previous illegal waste exports.
It called for a meeting next week of the federal states, who have been quarrelling over who should pay for the return transport, and the companies involved in the shipment.
